name: BARBADOS
lead: Barbados is a tiny coral island in the eastern Caribbean, only about 34 km long. It is the birthplace of rum. Its sugar once earned more than all of England's other colonies together. In 2021, it became a republic.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Barbados sits alone in the Atlantic, east of the other Caribbean islands. Unlike its volcanic neighbours, it is flat coral limestone. It rises to Mount Hillaby at 336 m.
The Scotland District in the north has rolling hills carved by rain. Calm beaches line the south and west. Surfers love the wild east coast.
animals: The flying fish is the national symbol. It leaps from the sea to escape predators. It glides on wing-like fins. Look for silver flashes from ferries at dawn.
About 10,000 green monkeys live here. People brought them from West Africa long ago. They raid mango trees. The Barbados bullfinch is the only bird found nowhere else.
culture: The national dish is flying fish with cou-cou, a creamy cornmeal-and-okra porridge. Cooks top it with steamed fish in tomato sauce. Rum shops stand on every corner.
Crop Over lasts from June to August. It has calypso contests and the Grand Kadooment, a costume parade through Bridgetown. Tuk bands play drums and penny whistles.
history: British settlers arrived in 1627 and planted sugar cane. By the late 1600s, tiny Barbados made more wealth than England's North American colonies together. Enslaved Africans did the brutal work.
Barbados won independence in 1966. On 30 November 2021, it peacefully became a republic. The British monarch is no longer head of state.
wows: Mount Gay has made rum since 1703, the oldest surviving rum brand.
The grapefruit was born in Barbados in the 1700s.
Barbados rarely gets hurricanes because it sits east of the main belt.
Barbados's Parliament began in 1639, the third oldest in the world.
Barbados has 1,500+ rum shops, about one per 185 residents.
Flying fish glide up to 45 m above the waves.
Rihanna, born here in 1988, became a National Hero in 2021.

myths.fact: Sugar cane is a giant grass. Workers crush its stalks to squeeze out sweet juice.
Rum comes from sugar cane juice or molasses, a thick syrup. Wine comes from grapes.
